name: Drawer
hint: Drag the header and flick: velocity decides whether it closes.
description: Side sheet or bottom sheet you can throw closed: release decides by distance and velocity, the bottom sheet snaps between half and full, and the backdrop fades with the drag. Holds any content: a title, a description, your children as the scrolling body and a pinned footer. Modal: focus trap, inert page behind, scroll lock, focus returns.
usage: Use for secondary tasks that keep page context (cart, filters, details, navigation on a phone). Pass `title`, `description`, the body as `children` and actions as `footer` (a node or ({ close, busy }) => node). Pick `side` (right, left, bottom) and `size` (sm, md, lg) or `width`. It opens from its own trigger button; pass `trigger` as your own element or `(props) => <Button {...props} />`, or control it with `open` / `onOpenChange` (opened by state with no `trigger`, it renders no button). Set `busy` while your save runs: the drawer cannot be closed until you clear it. On phones it becomes a bottom sheet; `sheetOnPhone={false}` keeps a side drawer. Keep the header as the drag handle so content can still scroll.

dataProps.description: The scrolling body: any content, or ({ close, busy }) => node. Empty by default; the gallery's cart appears only with `demo`.
Heading of the drawer; also its accessible name.
One line under the title, linked as the dialog's description.
Pinned actions under the body: any node, or ({ close, busy }) => node. None by default.
right, left or bottom. On phones every drawer is a bottom sheet unless sheetOnPhone is false.

sm, md or lg. Side sheets: 320, 400 or 560px wide (overrides width). Bottom sheets: hug the content up to half the screen, 88% of the screen, or 94%. Left unset, a bottom sheet hugs its content up to 88% of the screen.
Width of a side sheet in px (capped at the screen width).
On phones, turn a side drawer into a bottom sheet. false keeps it a side drawer, at most the screen width minus 48px.
Controlled open state. Leave undefined to let the drawer manage itself.
Open on mount when uncontrolled.
(open: boolean, reason) => void. reason: "trigger", "button" (Close), "drag", "footer" (your footer or children called close()), "escape" or "outside".
(reason) => void when the drawer closes, with the same reasons.
Escape closes the drawer.
A press on the backdrop closes the drawer.
Show the Close (X) button in the header. If you hide it, give the footer a way out.
Your own busy flag: Escape, outside press, Close and drag do nothing until it clears; the footer's close() still works.
Let the drawer close while busy.

Your own trigger: an element (cloned with a ref, onClick and aria attributes), or (props) => node spreading { ref, onClick, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, disabled }. Left out, a built-in button labelled `triggerLabel` shows, unless you pass `open`. null renders none.
Label of the built-in trigger button; also the drawer's name when there is no title.
Icon name on the built-in trigger button, or "none".
Disables the trigger so the drawer can't be opened from it.

Where focus goes on close: a ref, an element, a CSS selector or a function returning one. Default: the trigger, else what had focus before opening, else the control nearest to it. false leaves focus alone.
Show the gallery's cart when there are no children and no footer.
The dialog panel (null while closed). className, style and other props go to it too.

example:
<Drawer
  title="Filters"
  description="Narrow the list. Changes apply when you press Show."
  side="right"
  size="sm"
  trigger={<Button variant="secondary" label="Filters" />}
  footer={({ close }) => <Button label={`Show ${count} results`} fullWidth onClick={() => { apply(); close(); }} />}
>
  <FilterForm />
</Drawer>

{/* app navigation on a phone, opened by state */}
<Drawer
  side="left"
  sheetOnPhone={false}
  title="Menu"
  open={navOpen}
  onOpenChange={setNavOpen}
>
  <NavLinks onNavigate={() => setNavOpen(false)} />
</Drawer>
